_doc: Per-reviewer behavioral profile. Read by run_reviewers.sh (timeout, retry, model), the SKILL.md synthesis step (severity_priors, synthesis_weight), and analyze_runlog.sh (suggests edits to this file). Tune values here, not in scattered defaults. Edit notes/specialization freely; numeric tuning is best driven by analyze_runlog.sh suggestions over real runs. NOTE: antigravity and gemini-pro are BOTH served by Google's `agy` (Antigravity) CLI as of the 2026-06-18 Gemini-CLI sunset — the only difference is the --model value. The `model` field here MUST be the exact display-name string `agy models` prints (e.g. "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"); agy silently falls back to its default (Flash) on an unrecognized model string instead of erroring.

codex.specialization: general — fast-or-fail; agentic file roaming with built-in review prompt
codex.notes: Reliable in observed runs (4/4 most rounds). Treat solo P1 as near-certain real. Output sometimes truncates on very long sessions — surface the truncation in the runlog rather than retrying.

antigravity.specialization: architecture, side-effects, cross-file reasoning; agentic file-reading via Google's `agy` CLI on Gemini 3.5 Flash. Fast lap of the Gemini fleet. Rotation-pool member (not a baseline).
antigravity.notes: Replaces the prior `gemini` (Gemini CLI Flash) reviewer slot, retired in the 2026-06-18 Gemini-CLI consumer sunset. Binary: `agy` (install: `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash`, lands in ~/.local/bin; auth: `agy login` once). Model is pinned via `--model "Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)"` — must match an `agy models` display name exactly or agy silently uses its default. Solo findings have lower precision than convergent ones — weight accordingly. EMPTY OUTPUT: check meta.json failure_kind + the .agy.log tail before diagnosing — quota_exhausted (shared 'Individual quota', 429, resets on a ~2-day cadence; observed 2026-07-01: agy exits 0 with empty stdout in ~5s) is at least as common as expired `agy login` auth. NO FALLBACK (policy 2026-07-01): on quota/panic the lap drops out of the round; roster rotation covers the gap and the leaderboard down-weights it until it recovers.

gemini-pro.specialization: deep reasoning, multi-step logic, architectural and semantic-drift findings the Flash lap misses. Slower and more expensive than antigravity (Flash). Deep lap of the Gemini fleet. Rotation-pool member (not a baseline).
gemini-pro.notes: Same `agy` CLI as antigravity, just pinned to `--model "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"`. Previously routed through the standalone `gemini` CLI (-m gemini-3.1-pro-preview); migrated to agy in the 2026-06-18 sunset since agy now hosts Gemini 3.1 Pro and exposes --model. Pro is a preview tier — surface model-availability errors to the user, don't auto-retry. NOTE: antigravity + gemini-pro are the SAME provider (Google) — their agreement is NOT independent the way codex/kimi convergence is; treat Flash+Pro overlap as one provider's vote, not two. Pro triggers agy's SIGSEGV panic (RunCommandHandler nil-deref, agy ≤1.0.15) far more than Flash — it roams files/commands harder; exit 2 + ~20-45s + empty output = the panic, not your diff. Quota semantics: same as antigravity (check failure_kind). NO FALLBACK (policy 2026-07-01) — a failed lap drops out; rotation + leaderboard handle it.

kimi.specialization: single-turn correctness, race conditions, defensive guards; reasons on the diff as given without tools
kimi.notes: Strong on the diff-as-given. Frequent Low/nit output is skip-worthy unless convergent. China-origin provider — surface for security-sensitive repos.

kimi27.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning on Moonshot's code-specialized k2.7; rotation-pool member on the DIRECT Moonshot platform API (same billing rail as the kimi baseline, NOT OpenRouter).
kimi27.notes: Kimi k2.7-code via the direct Moonshot platform API (api.moonshot.ai/v1, key from MOONSHOT_API_KEY or ~/.config/moonshot/key). Added 2026-07-03 per Gabriel with draw_boost 2.5 so it would be drawn frequently while earning leaderboard data. Retired to draw_boost 1.0 on 2026-07-12 after reaching 10 sampled runs (score 72, 7/16 findings convergent) — now competes on the same footing as the rest of the pool. Same provider as the kimi baseline: kimi+kimi27 agreement counts as ONE provider vote at synthesis. China-origin provider (Moonshot) — surface for security-sensitive repos.

kimi3.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning on Moonshot's flagship Kimi K3 (2.8T MoE, 16/896 experts active, 1M context); rotation-pool member on the DIRECT Moonshot platform API (same billing rail as the kimi baseline and kimi27, NOT OpenRouter).
kimi3.notes: Kimi K3 via the direct Moonshot platform API (api.moonshot.ai/v1, model id `kimi-k3`, key from MOONSHOT_API_KEY or ~/.config/moonshot/key). Added 2026-07-18 per Gabriel, two days after Moonshot's 2026-07-16 K3 release — draw_boost 2.5 so it's drawn frequently while it earns leaderboard data; retire the boost after ~10 sampled runs per the kimi27 precedent. Full open weights weren't out yet at add-time (expected 2026-07-27) — this seat hits the hosted API, not local weights. Same provider as kimi/kimi27: kimi+kimi27+kimi3 agreement counts as ONE provider vote at synthesis. China-origin provider (Moonshot) — surface for security-sensitive repos.

glm.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning; independent provider vote (Zhipu). Rotation-pool member.
glm.notes: GLM 5.2 via the OpenRouter chat-completions API — no CLI, no agentic tools; the diff is inlined (8000-line cap, same as kimi). Requires an OpenRouter key ($OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ~/.config/openrouter/key); without one the wrapper skips it. Added 2026-07-01; verified live (caught a planted one-line bug as Critical on its first run). Priors start conservative (mirroring kimi); let leaderboard.sh data drive tuning. China-origin provider (Zhipu), routed through OpenRouter (US) — surface both for security-sensitive repos.

deepseek.specialization: single-turn diff reasoning, reasoning tier; independent provider vote (DeepSeek). Rotation-pool member. Also the designated OpenRouter substitute for the fact-check pass when agy is down.
deepseek.notes: DeepSeek V4 Pro (0813) via OpenRouter ($0.43/M in, $0.87/M out, 1M ctx). Added 2026-07-01 as V4 Flash; **upgraded to V4 Pro 2026-08-14** because the Flash seat was the worst paid performer on the board (score 52 over 6 runs — 3 findings, 0 convergent, 2 disproven). Pro is ~3x Flash's price and still among the cheapest paid seats; the bet is that the disproven rate was a capability floor, not a prompt problem. Reset expectations: treat pre-2026-08-14 deepseek leaderboard rows as a different model — and because the seat name is the leaderboard key, that reset is not automatic: draw_boost 2.5 was added 2026-08-14 so the score-52 Flash history stops suppressing the new model's chance to earn its own. Retire the boost after ~10 sampled runs, same as seed/grok. China-origin provider (DeepSeek), routed through OpenRouter (US) — surface both for security-sensitive repos.

_synthesis_rules.skip_unless_convergent: Drop a single-reviewer finding at this severity unless another reviewer flagged the same file/area.
_synthesis_rules.trust_if_convergent: Promote/keep when 2+ reviewers agree; downgrade or verify when solo.
_synthesis_rules.verify: Solo finding is worth a manual look but not auto-applied.
_synthesis_rules.high_precision: Solo finding still ranks; treat as near-certain real.
_synthesis_rules.medium_precision: Solo finding ranks but apply judgment; convergence boosts confidence.
_synthesis_rules.synthesis_weight_use: Tie-breaker when reviewers disagree on severity. Higher weight wins. Also used by analyze_runlog.sh to compute weighted reliability scores.
_synthesis_rules.provider_independence: antigravity and gemini-pro share the Google/Gemini provider — count their agreement as a single provider vote when judging convergence. True independent convergence means agreement ACROSS providers; each profile carries an explicit `provider` field (openai, google, moonshot, zhipu, deepseek, xiaomi, minimax, sakana, cohere, nvidia). OpenRouter is a ROUTER, not a provider: glm through OpenRouter is the Zhipu vote, nemotron is the NVIDIA vote, etc. With a rotating roster, 3+ distinct-provider agreement is the near-certain tier.
_synthesis_rules.rotation: codex and kimi are fixed baselines (`baseline: true`) — always on. Everything else is drawn per-round by select_roster.sh, weighted by leaderboard.sh scores (see those scripts for the formula). NO OpenRouter fallbacks for first-party reviewers (codex/gemini/claude — policy 2026-07-01): a failed lap drops out and rotation covers the gap.
